newsitem.title: GERMANY: German nuclear waste shipment sets off for dump.
newsitem.headline: German nuclear waste shipment sets off for dump.

text.p: A controversial nuclear waste shipment started the last leg of its journey on Wednesday to a dump in northern Germany, amid massive protests by hundreds of anti-nuclear activists.

The first of six flat-bed trucks carrying containers of spent fuel rods left a station in the town of Dannenberg under heavy police escort to ensure its safe arrival at Gorleben storage depot, 20 km (14 miles) away.
The first truck left the gates of the loading station but was forced to grind to a halt in front of a large cordon of police.
A short distance along the route to Gorleben protesters had chained themselves to a rope that was tied to trees on either side of the road, blocking the way for the nuclear waste convoy.
Activists had earlier burrowed underneath roads leading to Gorleben and set up barricades on others in an attempt to make them too dangerous for the flat-bed trucks to pass.

The convoy scheduled to leave early on Wednesday was delayed when 4,000 activists staged sit-down protests on the roads and riot police tried to clear the route to the depot by carrying them away individually and eventually firing water cannon on them.
